scope: Derived engineering and adversarial closure obligations for every atomic AIQ task.

inheritance_policy.rule: Each AIQ task inherits the union of engineering obligations and adversarial closure axes from every work_package_ref. Inheritance may only be reduced by an explicit, reviewable not-applicable disposition; task completion never erases capability-level promotion gates.
inheritance_policy.no_shortcut: A task may remain queue-complete for historical/accountability purposes while engineering or adversarial evidence is pending; such completion cannot be cited as verified/hardened/production proof.

adversarial_stop_conditions: AC-02: No hardened claim while shutdown can strand authority or repeat a side effect.
AC-03: A package cannot be production-ready if exhaustion becomes corruption, deadlock, or unbounded retry.
AC-05: Unknown side-effect outcome must enter reconciliation, not blind retry.
AC-06: Every durable projection/effect path must have a bounded reconciliation story.
AC-07: No strong promotion without a proven mixed-version window or an explicit stop-the-world contract.
AC-08: Restore is incomplete until deletion, identity, leases, and external effects are reconciled.
AC-09: Time-dependent authorization or ownership must not rely on unqualified wall-clock assumptions.
AC-14: Verified/hardened/production claims require artifact-bound, retained, independently checkable evidence.
AC-16: Core correctness may not depend on telemetry availability; critical recovery evidence must remain reconstructable.
AC-17: Tenant/workspace identity must be part of every authoritative lookup, cache key, receipt, and replay boundary.
AC-18: Derived state must be rebuildable from authoritative inputs without resurrecting forbidden or stale data.
AC-20: Promotion stops on unresolved target/current drift or machine/human contract disagreement.
AC-21: Critical recovery paths require an acyclic bootstrap or a documented dependency-reduced safe mode.
AC-23: No production claim based only on short-lived happy-path runs where aging changes semantics.
AC-24: Applicable critical compound campaigns must pass or carry explicit signed risk acceptance before production promotion.
tasks.implementation_packet_rule: Before implementation review, the task packet must disposition every inherited engineering dimension and adversarial closure axis and name concrete artifacts or explicit not-applicable rationale.
tasks.strong_promotion_rule: AIQ task completion is not equivalent to verified/hardened/production capability status. Strong promotion requires bound budgets, executable engineering and adversarial evidence, recovery/compatibility proof, compound-fault coverage where applicable, independent verification and signed accountability.
